outline: Disorders of sweat and sebaceous glands
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Hidradenitis suppurativa is a chronic, noncontagious inflammatory disorder that begins in hair follicles and produces recurrent painful nodules or boil-like lesions in areas where skin touches or rubs. Lesions can drain chronically, form interconnected tunnel-like tracts beneath the skin, and heal with scarring.
vignette: A 28-year-old woman has had recurrent painful lumps in both axillae and the groin for 4 years. Individual lesions enlarge, sometimes drain purulent-appearing material, and then partially improve, but new lesions continue to develop nearby. Examination shows several tender subcutaneous nodules, multiple depressed scars, and two narrow openings in the left axilla that communicate beneath the skin. Similar scarring is present in both inguinal folds. She is afebrile and otherwise well.
lead: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
distractor_notes: Staphylococcal boils can be painful, purulent, and recurrent and may occur in the axillae or thighs. However, the chronic bilateral intertriginous pattern with persistent scars and communicating subcutaneous tunnels is characteristic of hidradenitis suppurativa rather than recurrent isolated furuncles.

Folliculitis causes inflammation of individual hair follicles with superficial pimples or pustules and may occur in the groin. It does not best explain years of deep painful nodules with communicating tunnels and extensive scarring.

Epidermoid cysts are typically discrete, slow-growing subcutaneous lumps, often with a central punctum, and are usually painless unless inflamed or infected. Multiple cysts do not characteristically form the recurrent symmetric axillary/inguinal tunnel-and-scar pattern described here.

Severe nodular acne can produce deep painful nodules and scarring, but acne also characteristically includes follicular lesions such as comedones and most commonly affects acne-prone sites. The recurrent axillary and inguinal lesions with draining tunnels are more characteristic of hidradenitis suppurativa.
key_expl: This patient has hidradenitis suppurativa. NIAMS describes HS as a chronic inflammatory condition with painful bumps or boils in areas where skin touches or rubs, most commonly the armpits and groin. With more advanced disease, lesions can develop chronic drainage, interconnected tunnel-like structures beneath the skin, open wounds, and significant scarring. The combination of recurrent deep lesions in bilateral intertriginous areas plus tunnels and scars is therefore highly characteristic.
objective: Recognize hidradenitis suppurativa from recurrent painful intertriginous nodules or boils that progress to chronic drainage, subcutaneous tunnels, and scarring.

sources.title: Boils
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes boils/furuncles as infections, most commonly due to Staphylococcus aureus, involving groups of hair follicles and nearby skin; they may be painful, purulent, and recurrent.

sources.title: Folliculitis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes folliculitis as inflammation of hair follicles causing a rash and pimples or pustules near follicles, including in the groin.

sources.title: Epidermoid cyst
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes epidermoid cysts as discrete subcutaneous lumps that are usually slow-growing and painless, often with a central pit, although they may become inflamed or infected.
